statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-119376 is a stack exhaustion in SQLite: chained COLLATE operators were not counted against SQLITE_LIMIT_EXPR_DEPTH, so SQL or a view in an untrusted database with about 175,000 of them recurses without bound in sqlite3WalkExprNN() and crashes the process. SQLite lists it as fixed in 3.54.0: https://sqlite.org/cves.html, https://sqlite.org/bugs/info/2026-10-04T04:50:56Z. The fix is trunk check-in https://sqlite.org/src/info/252c0b7bf5a727d2, mirrored as https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/commit/d54522a5b832422ab893a1e9fa7a99ab314ea4e2, which fixes the expression-tree depth calculation for COLLATE; it is not in SQLite 3.53.4. DHI's 3.53.4-r1 build is SQLite 3.53.4 with a backport of that check-in. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes packages built from source sqlite (sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static, sqlite-dev and sqlite-doc) at 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0, 3.53.4-r0 and 3.53.4-r1, for x86_64 and aarch64. We unpacked the sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static and sqlite-dev packages of every one of those builds on both architectures, each checked against its index checksum. SQLite is compiled into three files in each build: the sqlite3 shell in the sqlite package, which carries its own copy and does not link libsqlite3; the shared library in sqlite-libs; and the static archive libsqlite3.a in sqlite-static. sqlite-dev holds only headers, a pkg-config file and the libsqlite3.so link. The shell and both libraries report SQLite 3.51.1, 3.51.2, 3.53.4 and 3.53.4 in those builds. The 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 builds are built from the upstream 3.51.1, 3.51.2 and 3.53.4 releases, none of which contains the fix. We ran the test with the sqlite3 shell, and with a test program linked once against the shared library and once against the static archive, for every build on x86_64 and aarch64. A SELECT with 1,500 chained COLLATE operators returns a row in 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 and fails with "Expression tree is too large (maximum depth 1000)" in 3.53.4-r1, on both architectures and in all three copies. The x86_64 runs used Docker Desktop's amd64 emulation. So 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 are affected and 3.53.4-r1 is fixed.
